genuine_findings_beyond_design_scope.finding: AC4 test mechanism bug found via mutation testing (not anticipated by the design doc): the first draft of the AC4 test monitored `pollers_pid_before` (captured BEFORE the manual terminate_child/restart_child used only to make Pollers re-read the :force_poller_crash/:start_scheduler env overrides) -- but `terminate_child/2` itself always produces a `:DOWN` for that pid regardless of whether any crash-loop ever happens, so the test passed even with the guard clause fully disabled (a false-positive test). Fixed by monitoring the PID CAPTURED AFTER the manual restart instead, so the asserted `:DOWN` can only come from the poller's OWN subsequent, automatic crash-loop-triggered exit. Documented in the test file's own comments.
genuine_findings_beyond_design_scope.finding_2: A second, more serious timing hazard found via the same mutation-testing pass, also not anticipated by the design: once the crash-looping Pollers layer exits and the top-level Letflow.Supervisor restarts it automatically, :force_poller_crash was still `true` in the freshly-restarted Pollers' env -- so the new instance immediately crash-looped AGAIN, fast enough to also exhaust the TOP-LEVEL supervisor's own default restart intensity (3/5s) and take the WHOLE :letflow application down mid-test (observed directly: `[notice] Application letflow exited: shutdown`). Fixed by clearing both `:force_poller_crash` and `:start_scheduler` immediately after observing the first `:DOWN`, which reliably wins the race against the top-level supervisor's own restart (which must still traverse Pollers.init/1 -> the Poller GenServer's own start_link/init -> its zero-delay first :tick, several BEAM message-passing hops the synchronously-resumed test process does not have to wait through) -- verified stable across 5 consecutive runs.
genuine_findings_beyond_design_scope.finding_3: Supervisor.which_children/1 returns children in REVERSE start order (OTP's own documented/observed behavior, each child prepended to the supervisor's internal list as it starts) -- test/letflow/supervisor/infrastructure_test.exs's ordering assertions reverse the raw result before comparing against the expected child-spec order. Not called out in the design doc; discovered when the first draft of that test failed against the real running tree.

genuine_findings_beyond_design_scope.finding: Design's own §9 Q4 (does :logger.add_primary_filter/2 raise on a duplicate filter id) is now EMPIRICALLY RESOLVED: this environment has a real Elixir/OTP toolchain the design environment did not. Running the AC2 cold-boot test WITHOUT its :logger.remove_primary_filter/1 defensive step (temporary local edit, reverted before committing) completed with no raise and no logged error on Elixir 1.20.3 / OTP 29 -- :logger.add_primary_filter/2 is a silent no-op (or ignored error return) on a duplicate id here, contradicting the original inline comment's own stated assumption in lib/letflow/application.ex ('raises on a duplicate filter id'). The defensive removal step is KEPT anyway, per the design's own stated reasoning (a no-op removal-then-readd is never a hazard either way, and it stays faithful to that comment's 'exactly once per node' assumption rather than relying on one runtime's observed-but-undocumented behavior). Documented in test/letflow/supervisor/pollers_test.exs's own moduledoc.

5 pre-existing test files/helpers referenced Letflow.Supervisor directly for children that moved one layer down under this design (Letflow.Admission, Oidcc.ProviderConfiguration.Worker, Letflow.Engine.PluginRegistry all moved into Letflow.Supervisor.Infrastructure; scheduler_children/0 and service_task_dispatcher_children/0's own source moved into Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers). These were NOT enumerated in the design doc's §8 test-file summary (which focused only on the 3 new test files) and were NOT flagged as needing changes anywhere in the design or its two CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR passes. Fixing them was necessary for `mix test` to pass at all (a direct AC10 requirement) and was done as the minimal retargeting needed (Letflow.Supervisor -> Letflow.Supervisor.Infrastructure at each call site), not a redesign of those tests. Flagged here explicitly for REVIEWER since it is a deviation from 'implement exactly what the design says and nothing else' -- it was a necessary, mechanical consequence of the design's own approved restructuring, not an independent design decision.

security_review_routing_decision.rationale: Checked docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md's actual INV-1..INV-9 criteria against this change: no new API route, no migration, no secrets handling, no response shaping, no tenant-scoped query, and no new data-access path is introduced -- this is purely an OTP supervision-tree restructuring plus one test-only, double-gated (compile-time AND runtime) guard clause that raises inside an already-existing GenServer's already-existing tick handler. None of INV-1 (tenant isolation), INV-2 (field authorization), INV-4 (secrets by reference), INV-6 (new data-access path), INV-7 (SQL interpolation), or INV-9 (outbound URL validation) apply. This is a REVIEWER-critical OTP-idiom/availability change (per the task brief), not a tenant-data-path change, so SECURITY-REVIEWER is correctly skipped.
